label: early-position detector: input steps t=1..4
explanation: Purely positional feature. Fires on every sequence at steps t=1,2,3 (any input, including the <DEL> at t=3 when L=3) and at t=4 when it is still an original token (not the L=4 delimiter). Silent at t=0, at t>=5 (except a rare weak trace at t=5), and in the copy phase. Token identity, L, first token, and history do not matter (rates are flat across tokens). Magnitude depends on position: highest at t=2 (~1.0 of max), then t=1 (~0.8), t=3 (~0.55-0.6), and weak at t=4 (~0.15-0.25). Within a position, magnitude varies a little with the earlier tokens.

issues: Minor: 'silent throughout the copy phase' is not literally true. 23 copy-phase activations show up on dev, at recall_idx 2 (t=5 when L=3). This is negligible.

Minor: the t=5 trace (about 2.5k steps per split, around 0.08-0.11 of max, 0.0% of the activation mass) follows the same pattern every time: t=5 when it is still an original token, so L>=6. It is a weak extension of the position ramp, not a separate class. Adding t==5 to the predicate drops precision to 0.79 (test F1 0.885), so leaving it out is correct.
Minor: the test false positives (90 steps, all at t=4 with original tokens, preceded by a normal t=1..3 ramp) look like threshold noise on the weak t=4 activation.

The label 'input steps t=1..4' simplifies slightly: it leaves out that the L=3 delimiter at t=3 counts and that the L=4 delimiter at t=4 does not. The explanation and predicate state both details correctly.
